train.explanation: Global conflict from 1939-1945 that reshaped the modern world and remains history's deadliest war
train.en: World War II (1939-1945), the most devastating global conflict in human history, fundamentally transformed the political, social, and economic landscape of the modern world while claiming an estimated 70-85 million lives. Beginning with Germany's invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939, the war expanded rapidly across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Pacific, involving virtually every nation and dividing the world into the Allied Powers (primarily Britain, Soviet Union, United States, and China) against the Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, and Japan). The conflict witnessed unprecedented industrial warfare, technological innovations including radar and nuclear weapons, and horrific atrocities such as the Holocaust, which systematically murdered six million Jews and millions of other victims. The war's conclusion in 1945, marked by Germany's surrender in May and Japan's capitulation following the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, ushered in a new world order dominated by the United States and Soviet Union, setting the stage for the Cold War and establishing the United Nations as humanity's attempt to prevent such catastrophic warfare from recurring.
train.en-rus: World War II (1939-1945), самый devastating global conflict в человеческой истории, fundamentally transformed политический, социальный, и экономический landscape современного мира while claiming приблизительно 70-85 миллионов жизней. Beginning с Germany's invasion Poland 1 сентября 1939, война expanded быстро across Europe, Asia, Africa, и Pacific, involving практически каждую nation и dividing мир на Allied Powers (в основном Britain, Soviet Union, United States, и China) против Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, и Japan). The conflict witnessed беспрецедентную industrial warfare, technological innovations including radar и nuclear weapons, и horrific atrocities такие как Holocaust, который systematically murdered шесть миллионов евреев и миллионы других victims. The war's заключение в 1945, marked Germany's surrender в мае и Japan's capitulation following atomic bombings Hiroshima и Nagasaki, ushered новый world order dominated United States и Soviet Union, setting stage для Cold War и establishing United Nations как humanity's attempt предотвратить такую catastrophic warfare от recurring.
train.en-zho: World War II (1939-1945), 人类历史上最具毁灭性的全球冲突, fundamentally transformed 现代世界的政治、社会和经济格局 while claiming 估计7000-8500万人的生命. Beginning 德国于1939年9月1日入侵波兰, 战争rapidly expanded across 欧洲、亚洲、非洲和太平洋, involving 几乎每个国家 and dividing 世界为同盟国(主要是英国、苏联、美国和中国) against 轴心国(德国、意大利和日本). The conflict witnessed 前所未有的工业化战争, technological innovations including 雷达和核武器, 以及可怖的暴行如大屠杀, 它systematically murdered 600万犹太人和数百万其他受害者. The war's 1945年的结束, marked 德国5月投降和日本在广岛长崎原子弹轰炸后投降, ushered 由美国和苏联主导的新世界秩序, setting stage 冷战并establishing 联合国作为人类防止此类灾难性战争再次发生的尝试.

Beginning ドイツの Poland 侵攻で1939年9月1日に, 戦争は rapidly expanded Europe, Asia, Africa, そして Pacific を across し, virtually すべての nation を involving し世界を Allied Powers (主に Britain, Soviet Union, United States, そして China) と Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, そして Japan) に dividing しました. The conflict は unprecedented な industrial warfare, radar や nuclear weapons を including する technological innovations, そして Holocaust のような horrific atrocities を witnessed し, それは systematically 600万人のユダヤ人と数百万の他の victims を murdered しました. The war の1945年の conclusion, Germany の5月の surrender と Hiroshima と Nagasaki への atomic bombings に following する Japan の capitulation で marked され, United States と Soviet Union に dominated される新しい world order を ushered し, Cold War の stage を setting し United Nations を humanity の such catastrophic warfare が recurring することを prevent する attempt として establishing しました.

train.en-spa: World War II (1939-1945), el más devastating global conflict en la historia humana, fundamentally transformed el political, social, y economic landscape del mundo moderno while claiming aproximadamente 70-85 millones de lives. train.en-fra: World War II (1939-1945), le plus devastating global conflict de l'histoire humaine, fundamentally transformed le paysage politique, social, et économique du monde moderne while claiming environ 70-85 millions de lives. Beginning avec l'invasion de la Poland par l'Germany le 1er septembre 1939, la guerre expanded rapidement across l'Europe, l'Asie, l'Afrique, et le Pacific, involving virtuellement chaque nation et dividing le monde en Allied Powers (principalement Britain, Soviet Union, United States, et China) contre les Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, et Japan). The conflict witnessed une warfare industrielle unprecedented, des technological innovations including radar et nuclear weapons, et des horrific atrocities comme l'Holocaust, qui systematically murdered six millions de juifs et des millions d'autres victims. The war's conclusion en 1945, marked par la surrender de l'Germany en mai et la capitulation du Japan following les atomic bombings d'Hiroshima et Nagasaki, ushered un nouvel world order dominated par les United States et Soviet Union, setting la stage pour la Cold War et establishing les United Nations comme l'attempt de l'humanity de prevent une telle catastrophic warfare de recurring.
train.en-ita: World War II (1939-1945), il più devastating global conflict nella storia umana, fundamentally transformed il paesaggio politico, sociale, ed economico del mondo moderno while claiming circa 70-85 milioni di lives. Beginning con l'invasion della Poland da parte della Germany il 1° settembre 1939, la guerra expanded rapidamente across Europa, Asia, Africa, e il Pacific, involving virtualmente ogni nation e dividing il mondo negli Allied Powers (principalmente Britain, Soviet Union, United States, e China) contro gli Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, e Japan). The conflict witnessed unprecedented industrial warfare, technological innovations including radar e nuclear weapons, e horrific atrocities come l'Holocaust, che systematically murdered sei milioni di ebrei e milioni di altre victims. The war's conclusione nel 1945, marked dalla surrender della Germany a maggio e dalla capitulation del Japan following gli atomic bombings di Hiroshima e Nagasaki, ushered un nuovo world order dominated dagli United States e Soviet Union, setting la stage per la Cold War e establishing le United Nations come l'attempt dell'humanity di prevent tale catastrophic warfare dal recurring.
train.en-tha: World War II (1939-1945), global conflict ที่ devastating ที่สุดในประวัติศาสตร์มนุษย์, fundamentally transformed ภูมิทัศน์ทางการเมือง สังคม และเศรษฐกิจของโลกสมัยใหม่ while claiming ประมาณ 70-85 ล้านชีวิต. Beginning ด้วยการบุกรุกโปแลนด์ของเยอรมนีเมื่อ 1 กันยายน 1939, สงครามได้ expanded อย่างรวดเร็ว across ยุโรป เอเชีย แอฟริกา และมหาสมุทรแปซิฟิก, involving เกือบทุกประเทศ และ dividing โลกเป็นฝ่าย Allied Powers (หลักๆ คือ อังกฤษ สหภาพโซเวียต สหรัฐอเมริกา และจีน) ต่อสู้กับ Axis Powers (เยอรมนี อิตาลี และญี่ปุ่น). The conflict witnessed สงครามอุตสาหกรรมที่ unprecedented, technological innovations including เรดาร์และอาวุธนิวเคลียร์, และ horrific atrocities เช่น Holocaust ซึ่ง systematically murdered ชาวยิวหกล้านคนและเหยื่ออื่นๆ อีกหลายล้านคน. The war's การสิ้นสุดใน 1945, marked โดยการยอมแพ้ของเยอรมนีในเดือนพฤษภาคมและการยอมแพ้ของญี่ปุ่น following การทิ้งระเบิดปรมาณูที่ฮิโรชิมาและนางาซากิ, ushered ระเบียบโลกใหม่ที่ dominated โดยสหรัฐอเมริกาและสหภาพโซเวียต, setting เวทีสำหรับสงครามเย็นและ establishing สหประชาชาติเป็น humanity's attempt เพื่อ prevent สงครามหายนะเช่นนี้จากการ recurring.
train.en-arb: World War II (1939-1945)، الصراع العالمي الأكثر تدميراً في التاريخ البشري، fundamentally transformed المشهد السياسي والاجتماعي والاقتصادي للعالم الحديث while claiming ما يقدر بـ 70-85 مليون حياة. Beginning بغزو ألمانيا لبولندا في 1 سبتمبر 1939، الحرب expanded بسرعة across أوروبا وآسيا وأفريقيا والمحيط الهادئ، involving تقريباً كل دولة و dividing العالم إلى قوى الحلفاء (بشكل أساسي بريطانيا والاتحاد السوفيتي والولايات المتحدة والصين) ضد قوى المحور (ألمانيا وإيطاليا واليابان). The conflict witnessed حرباً صناعية لم يسبق لها مثيل، technological innovations including الرادار والأسلحة النووية، و horrific atrocities مثل الهولوكوست، الذي systematically murdered ستة ملايين يهودي وملايين الضحايا الآخرين. The war's ختام في 1945، marked باستسلام ألمانيا في مايو واستسلام اليابان following القصف الذري لهيروشيما وناغازاكي، ushered نظاماً عالمياً جديداً dominated بالولايات المتحدة والاتحاد السوفيتي، setting المسرح للحرب الباردة و establishing الأمم المتحدة كمحاولة البشرية لـ prevent مثل هذه الحرب الكارثية من recurring.
train.en-tur: World War II (1939-1945), insan tarihindeki en devastating global çatışma, fundamentally transformed modern dünyanın siyasi, sosyal ve ekonomik manzarasını while claiming tahminen 70-85 milyon hayatı. Beginning Almanya'nın 1 Eylül 1939'da Polonya'yı işgaliyle, savaş rapidly expanded Avrupa, Asya, Afrika ve Pasifik'te, involving neredeyse her ulusu ve dünyayı Allied Powers (esas olarak İngiltere, Sovyetler Birliği, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri ve Çin) ile Axis Powers (Almanya, İtalya ve Japonya) arasında dividing etti. The conflict witnessed eşi görülmemiş endüstriyel savaş, radar ve nükleer silahlar including teknolojik yenilikler ve Holocaust gibi korkunç zulümler, bu systematically altı milyon Yahudi ve milyonlarca başka kurbanı murdered etti. The war's 1945'teki sonucu, Almanya'nın Mayıs'taki teslimi ve Japonya'nın Hiroshima ve Nagazaki'ye atom bombası atılması following capitulation'ıyla marked, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri ve Sovyetler Birliği tarafından dominated yeni bir dünya düzeni ushered etti, Soğuk Savaş için stage setting ve Birleşmiş Milletler'i böyle catastrophic savaşın recurring'ini prevent etmek için humanity'nin girişimi olarak establishing etti.
train.en-kor: World War II (1939-1945), 인류 역사상 가장 devastating한 global conflict, fundamentally transformed 현대 세계의 정치적, 사회적, 경제적 landscape를 while claiming 추정 7천만-8천5백만 lives를. Beginning 독일의 1939년 9월 1일 폴란드 침공으로, 전쟁은 rapidly expanded across 유럽, 아시아, 아프리카, 그리고 태평양, involving 거의 모든 nation과 dividing 세계를 연합국 (주로 영국, 소련, 미국, 그리고 중국) against 추축국 (독일, 이탈리아, 그리고 일본)으로. The conflict witnessed 전례없는 industrial warfare, technological innovations including 레이다와 핵무기, 그리고 홀로코스트 같은 horrific atrocities, 이것이 systematically murdered 6백만 유대인과 수백만 다른 victims를. The war's 1945년 conclusion, marked 독일의 5월 항복과 히로시마와 나가사키 atomic bombings following 일본의 capitulation으로, ushered 미국과 소련이 dominated하는 새로운 world order를, setting 냉전의 stage와 establishing 유엔을 humanity의 그런 catastrophic warfare가 recurring하는 것을 prevent하려는 attempt로.
train.en-hin: World War II (1939-1945), मानव इतिहास में सबसे devastating global conflict, fundamentally transformed आधुनिक दुनिया के political, social, और economic landscape को while claiming अनुमानित 70-85 मिलियन lives। Beginning Germany के Poland invasion के साथ 1 सितंबर 1939 को, युद्ध rapidly expanded across Europe, Asia, Africa, और Pacific, involving लगभग हर nation और dividing दुनिया को Allied Powers (मुख्यतः Britain, Soviet Union, United States, और China) में against Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, और Japan)। The conflict witnessed unprecedented industrial warfare, technological innovations including radar और nuclear weapons, और horrific atrocities जैसे Holocaust, जिसने systematically murdered छह मिलियन यहूदियों और मिलियनों अन्य victims को। The war का conclusion 1945 में, marked Germany के surrender मई में और Japan के capitulation के साथ following atomic bombings Hiroshima और Nagasaki के, ushered एक नया world order जो dominated था United States और Soviet Union से, setting stage Cold War के लिए और establishing United Nations को humanity के attempt के रूप में ऐसे catastrophic warfare को recurring से prevent करने के लिए।
train.en-ben: World War II (1939-1945), মানব ইতিহাসের সবচেয়ে devastating global conflict, fundamentally transformed আধুনিক বিশ্বের political, social, এবং economic landscape while claiming আনুমানিক 70-85 মিলিয়ন lives। Beginning জার্মানির পোল্যান্ড invasion দিয়ে 1 সেপ্টেম্বর 1939-এ, যুদ্ধ rapidly expanded across ইউরোপ, এশিয়া, আফ্রিকা, এবং প্রশান্ত মহাসাগর, involving প্রায় প্রতিটি nation এবং dividing বিশ্বকে Allied Powers (প্রধানত ব্রিটেন, সোভিয়েত ইউনিয়ন, যুক্তরাষ্ট্র, এবং চীন) against Axis Powers (জার্মানি, ইতালি, এবং জাপান)। The conflict witnessed অভূতপূর্ব industrial warfare, technological innovations including রাডার এবং nuclear weapons, এবং horrific atrocities যেমন Holocaust, যা systematically murdered ছয় মিলিয়ন ইহুদি এবং লক্ষ লক্ষ অন্যান্য victims। The war এর conclusion 1945 সালে, marked জার্মানির মে মাসে surrender এবং জাপানের capitulation following হিরোশিমা এবং নাগাসাকির atomic bombings, ushered একটি নতুন world order যা dominated ছিল যুক্তরাষ্ট্র এবং সোভিয়েত ইউনিয়ন দ্বারা, setting stage Cold War এর জন্য এবং establishing United Nations কে humanity এর attempt হিসেবে এমন catastrophic warfare recurring থেকে prevent করার জন্য।
train.en-tel: World War II (1939-1945), మానవ చరిత్రలో అత్యంత devastating global conflict, fundamentally transformed ఆధునిక ప్రపంచం యొక్క political, social, మరియు economic landscape ను while claiming అంచనాగా 70-85 మిలియన్ lives ను. Beginning జర్మనీ యొక్క పోలాండ్ invasion తో సెప్టెంబర్ 1, 1939న, యుద్ధం rapidly expanded across యూరప్, ఆసియా, ఆఫ్రికా, మరియు పసిఫిక్, involving దాదాపు ప్రతి nation ను మరియు dividing ప్రపంచాన్ని Allied Powers (ప్రధానంగా బ్రిటన్, సోవియట్ యూనియన్, యునైటెడ్ స్టేట్స్, మరియు చైనా) against Axis Powers (జర్మనీ, ఇటలీ, మరియు జపాన్). The conflict witnessed అపూర్వమైన industrial warfare, technological innovations including రాడార్ మరియు nuclear weapons, మరియు horrific atrocities అయిన Holocaust వంటివి, ఇది systematically murdered ఆరు మిలియన్ యూదులను మరియు మిలియన్ల ఇతర victims ను. The war యొక్క conclusion 1945లో, marked జర్మనీ యొక్క మే లో surrender మరియు జపాన్ యొక్క capitulation following హిరోషిమా మరియు నాగసాకి యొక్క atomic bombings, ushered ఒక కొత్త world order ను యునైటెడ్ స్టేట్స్ మరియు సోవియట్ యూనియన్ చేత dominated, setting stage Cold War కొరకు మరియు establishing United Nations ను humanity యొక్క attempt గా అలాంటి catastrophic warfare ను recurring నుండి prevent చేయడానికి.
train.en-swa: World War II (1939-1945), mapigano ya kimataifa yenye uharibifu mkubwa zaidi katika historia ya binadamu, fundamentally transformed mazingira ya kisiasa, kijamii, na kiuchumi ya ulimwengu wa kisasa huku yakidai maisha ya takribani milioni 70-85. Beginning na uvamizi wa Ujerumani nchini Poland tarehe 1 Septemba 1939, vita viliexpand haraka katika Ulaya, Asia, Afrika, na Pasifiki, vikihusisha hata taifa lolote na kugawanya ulimwengu katika Allied Powers (hasa Uingereza, Umoja wa Kisoviet, Marekani, na China) dhidi ya Axis Powers (Ujerumani, Italia, na Japan). The conflict viliwashuhudia vita vya viwandani visivyowahi kutokea, uvumbuzi wa kiteknolojia ukijumuisha rada na silaha za nyuklia, na ukatili wa kutisha kama Holocaust, ambayo iliua kwa mpango milioni sita ya Wayahudi na mamilioni ya wahanga wengine. Mwisho wa vita mnamo 1945, uliotiwa alama na kujitolea kwa Ujerumani mwezi Mei na kujitolea kwa Japan baada ya mapigo ya kivumba vya Hiroshima na Nagasaki, ulianzisha mpangilio mpya wa kimataifa uliotawaliwa na Marekani na Umoja wa Kisoviet, ukiweka jukwaa la Vita Baridi na kuanzisha Umoja wa Mataifa kama jaribio la binadamu la kuzuia vita vya msiba kama hivi vikarudi.
train.fa: جنگ جهانی دوم (۱۹۳۹-۱۹۴۵)، ویرانگرترین درگیری جهانی در تاریخ بشر، به طور بنیادی چشم‌انداز سیاسی، اجتماعی و اقتصادی جهان مدرن را دگرگون کرد و در عین حال جان حدود ۷۰ تا ۸۵ میلیون نفر را گرفت. این جنگ با حمله آلمان به لهستان در اول سپتامبر ۱۹۳۹ آغاز شد و به سرعت در سراسر اروپا، آسیا، آفریقا و اقیانوس آرام گسترش یافت، تقریباً تمام کشورها را درگیر کرد و جهان را به دو قطب متحدان (عمدتاً بریتانیا، اتحاد جماهیر شوروی، ایالات متحده و چین) در مقابل قدرت‌های محور (آلمان، ایتالیا و ژاپن) تقسیم کرد. این درگیری شاهد جنگ صنعتی بی‌سابقه، نوآوری‌های تکنولوژیکی از جمله رادار و سلاح‌های هسته‌ای، و جنایات وحشتناکی مانند هولوکاست بود که به طور سیستماتیک شش میلیون یهودی و میلیون‌ها قربانی دیگر را کشت. پایان جنگ در ۱۹۴۵، که با تسلیم آلمان در می و تسلیم ژاپن پس از بمباران اتمی هیروشیما و ناگازاکی مشخص شد، نظم جهانی جدیدی را به وجود آورد که تحت سلطه ایالات متحده و اتحاد شوروی بود، زمینه را برای جنگ سرد فراهم کرد و سازمان ملل متحد را به عنوان تلاش بشریت برای جلوگیری از تکرار چنین جنگ فاجعه‌باری تأسیس کرد.
train.tur: İkinci Dünya Savaşı (1939-1945), insanlık tarihinin en yıkıcı küresel çatışması olarak, modern dünyanın siyasi, sosyal ve ekonomik manzarasını temelden dönüştürmüş ve tahminen 70-85 milyon can kaybına neden olmuştur. 1 Eylül 1939'da Almanya'nın Polonya'yı işgaliyle başlayan savaş, Avrupa, Asya, Afrika ve Pasifik'e hızla yayılarak neredeyse her ulusu içine çekmiş ve dünyayı Müttefik Güçler (başta İngiltere, Sovyetler Birliği, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri ve Çin) ile Mihver Güçleri (Almanya, İtalya ve Japonya) arasında ikiye bölmüştür. Çatışma, eşi görülmemiş endüstriyel savaş, radar ve nükleer silahlar dahil teknolojik yenilikler ve altı milyon Yahudi ile milyonlarca başka kurbanı sistematik olarak öldüren Holokost gibi korkunç zulümlere tanık olmuştur. 1945'te savaşın sona ermesi, Mayıs'ta Almanya'nın teslim olması ve Hiroşima ile Nagazaki'ye atom bombası atılmasının ardından Japonya'nın kapitülasyonuyla, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri ve Sovyetler Birliği'nin egemenliğindeki yeni bir dünya düzeni başlatmış, Soğuk Savaş'ın sahnesini hazırlamış ve böylesi felaketli savaşların tekrarlanmasını önleme girişimi olarak Birleşmiş Milletler'i kurmuştur.
train.ita: La Seconda Guerra Mondiale (1939-1945), il conflitto globale più devastante della storia umana, ha trasformato radicalmente il panorama politico, sociale ed economico del mondo moderno causando una stima di 70-85 milioni di vittime. Iniziata con l'invasione tedesca della Polonia il 1° settembre 1939, la guerra si espanse rapidamente attraverso Europa, Asia, Africa e Pacifico, coinvolgendo virtualmente ogni nazione e dividendo il mondo tra le Potenze Alleate (principalmente Gran Bretagna, Unione Sovietica, Stati Uniti e Cina) contro le Potenze dell'Asse (Germania, Italia e Giappone). Il conflitto fu testimone di una guerra industriale senza precedenti, innovazioni tecnologiche inclusi radar e armi nucleari, e atroci atrocità come l'Olocausto, che assassinò sistematicamente sei milioni di ebrei e milioni di altre vittime. La conclusione della guerra nel 1945, segnata dalla resa della Germania a maggio e dalla capitolazione del Giappone seguita ai bombardamenti atomici di Hiroshima e Nagasaki, inaugurò un nuovo ordine mondiale dominato da Stati Uniti e Unione Sovietica, preparando il terreno per la Guerra Fredda e stabilendo le Nazioni Unite come tentativo dell'umanità di prevenire il ricorrere di guerre così catastrofiche.
train.zho: 第二次世界大战（1939-1945年）是人类历史上最具破坏性的全球冲突，从根本上改变了现代世界的政治、社会和经济格局，夺去了约7000-8500万人的生命。战争始于1939年9月1日德国入侵波兰，迅速扩展到欧洲、亚洲、非洲和太平洋地区，几乎涉及每一个国家，将世界分为同盟国（主要是英国、苏联、美国和中国）对抗轴心国（德国、意大利和日本）。这场冲突见证了前所未有的工业化战争、包括雷达和核武器在内的技术创新，以及大屠杀等可怕暴行，系统性地杀害了600万犹太人和数百万其他受害者。战争于1945年结束，以德国在5月投降和日本在广岛、长崎原子弹轰炸后投降为标志，开创了由美国和苏联主导的新世界秩序，为冷战奠定了基础，并建立了联合国作为人类防止此类灾难性战争再次发生的尝试。

train.explanation: Austrian neurologist who founded psychoanalysis and revolutionized understanding of the human mind
train.en: Sigmund Freud (1856-1939), born in Freiberg, Moravia, revolutionized modern psychology and forever changed humanity's understanding of the unconscious mind through his groundbreaking development of psychoanalysis. Working initially as a neurologist in Vienna, Freud pioneered the exploration of repressed memories, dreams, and unconscious desires, proposing that human behavior is largely driven by unconscious forces and childhood experiences. His revolutionary theories included the structural model of the psyche (id, ego, and superego), the Oedipus complex, and the interpretation of dreams as the "royal road to the unconscious," challenging Victorian sensibilities by emphasizing the central role of sexuality in human psychology. Despite facing significant criticism and controversy throughout his career, particularly regarding his emphasis on sexual drives and his methods of treatment, Freud's influence extended far beyond clinical psychology, profoundly impacting literature, anthropology, sociology, and popular culture, making psychoanalytic concepts like defense mechanisms, transference, and the talking cure fundamental to modern therapeutic practice and our understanding of mental health.

train.en-tha: Sigmund Freud (1856-1939), เกิดใน Freiberg, Moravia, revolutionized จิตวิทยาสมัยใหม่ และ forever changed ความเข้าใจของมนุษยชาติเกี่ยวกับ unconscious mind ผ่าน groundbreaking development ของ psychoanalysis. Despite facing การวิจารณ์อย่างมากและความขัดแย้ง throughout อาชีพของเขา, particularly regarding การเน้นของเขาใน sexual drives และ methods การรักษาของเขา, Freud's influence extended ไกลเกิน clinical psychology, profoundly impacting วรรณกรรม, มานุษยวิทยา, สังคมวิทยา, และวัฒนธรรมป๊อป, making แนวคิด psychoanalytic เช่น defense mechanisms, transference, และ talking cure เป็น fundamental ต่อ modern therapeutic practice และความเข้าใจของเราเกี่ยวกับ mental health.
train.en-arb: Sigmund Freud (1856-1939)، المولود في فرايبرغ، مورافيا، revolutionized علم النفس الحديث و forever changed فهم البشرية للعقل اللاواعي من خلال تطويره الرائد للتحليل النفسي. Working في البداية كطبيب أعصاب في فيينا، Freud pioneered استكشاف الذكريات المكبوتة والأحلام والرغبات اللاواعية، proposing أن السلوك البشري مدفوع بشكل كبير بالقوى اللاواعية وتجارب الطفولة. His النظريات الثورية included النموذج الهيكلي للنفس (الهو والأنا والأنا العليا)، عقدة أوديب، وتفسير الأحلام كـ"الطريق الملكي إلى اللاوعي"، challenging الحساسيات الفيكتورية من خلال التأكيد على الدور المركزي للجنسانية في علم النفس البشري. Despite facing انتقادات كبيرة وجدلاً throughout مسيرته المهنية، particularly regarding تركيزه على الدوافع الجنسية وطرق العلاج، تأثير فرويد extended far beyond علم النفس السريري، مؤثراً بعمق على الأدب والأنثروبولوجيا وعلم الاجتماع والثقافة الشعبية، making المفاهيم التحليلية النفسية مثل آليات الدفاع والنقل والعلاج بالكلام أساسية للممارسة العلاجية الحديثة وفهمنا للصحة النفسية.
train.en-tur: Sigmund Freud (1856-1939), Freiberg, Moravya'da doğdu, modern psikolojiyi devrimleştirdi ve psikanaliz alanındaki çığır açan gelişimi sayesinde insanlığın bilinçsiz zihin anlayışını sonsuza dek değiştirdi. Vienna'da başlangıçta nörolog olarak çalışan Freud, bastırılmış anılar, rüyalar ve bilinçsiz arzuların keşfine öncülük etti, insan davranışının büyük ölçüde bilinçsiz güçler ve çocukluk deneyimleri tarafından yönlendirildiğini öne sürdü. Devrimci teorileri arasında psişenin yapısal modeli (id, ego ve süperego), Oedipus kompleksi ve rüyaların bilinçsizliğe giden "krali yol" olarak yorumlanması yer aldı, Viktorya döneminin hassasiyetlerine meydan okuyarak insan psikolojisinde cinselliğin merkezi rolünü vurguladı. Kariyeri boyunca özellikle cinsel dürtülere verdiği önem ve tedavi yöntemleri konusunda önemli eleştiri ve tartışmalarla karşılaştığı halde, Freud'un etkisi klinik psikolojinin çok ötesine uzandı, edebiyat, antropoloji, sosyoloji ve popüler kültürü derinden etkiledi, savunma mekanizmaları, aktarım ve konuşma tedavisi gibi psikanalitik kavramları modern terapötik uygulamalara ve ruh sağlığı anlayışımıza temel hale getirdi.
train.en-kor: Sigmund Freud (1856-1939), born 프라이베르크, 모라비아에서, revolutionized 현대 심리학을 and forever changed 인류의 무의식 정신에 대한 이해를 through 그의 정신분석학의 groundbreaking development. Working 처음에 비엔나에서 신경학자로, Freud pioneered 억압된 기억, 꿈, 그리고 무의식적 욕망의 탐구를, proposing 인간 행동이 largely driven 무의식적 힘과 유년기 경험에 의해. His revolutionary theories included 정신의 구조적 모델 (이드, 자아, 초자아), 오이디푸스 콤플렉스, 그리고 꿈의 해석을 무의식으로의 "왕도"로, challenging 빅토리아 시대의 감수성을 by emphasizing 인간 심리학에서 성의 중심적 역할을. Despite facing 그의 경력 throughout 상당한 비판과 논란을, particularly regarding 성적 충동에 대한 그의 강조와 치료 방법들, Freud's influence extended 임상 심리학을 far beyond, profoundly impacting 문학, 인류학, 사회학, 그리고 대중문화를, making 방어기제, 전이, 그리고 대화 치료 같은 정신분석적 개념들을 modern therapeutic practice와 정신 건강에 대한 우리의 이해에 fundamental하게.

train.en-swa: Sigmund Freud (1856-1939), aliyezaliwa Freiberg, Moravia, alirevolutionize psychology ya kisasa na forever changed uelewa wa binadamu wa akili isiyotambulika kupitia maendeleo yake ya kipekee ya psychoanalysis. Akifanya kazi mwanzoni kama daktari wa neva huko Vienna, Freud alianzisha uchunguzi wa kumbukumbu zilizofichwa, ndoto, na hamu zisizotambulika, akipendekeza kwamba tabia ya binadamu inaongozwa kwa kiasi kikubwa na nguvu zisizotambulika na uzoefu wa utotoni. Nadharia zake za mapinduzi zilizojumuisha muundo wa kiakili (id, ego, na superego), utata wa Oedipus, na ufafanuzi wa ndoto kama "barabara ya kifalme kuelekea kisicho na utambuzi," akipinga hisia za Victorian kwa kusisitiza jukumu kuu la uume na uke katika psychology ya binadamu. Licha ya kukabiliana na ukosoaji mkubwa na mafarakano katika kazi yake yote, hasa kuhusu msisitizo wake kwenye mipigo ya kijinsia na njia zake za matibabu, ushawishi wa Freud ulienea mbali zaidi ya psychology ya kliniki, ukiathiri kwa undani fasihi, anthropology, sociology, na utamaduni wa kijamii, na kufanya dhana za psychoanalytic kama taratibu za ulinzi, uhamishaji, na matibabu ya mazungumzo kuwa za kimsingi kwa mazoezi ya kisasa ya matibabu na uelewa wetu wa afya ya kiakili.
train.fa: زیگموند فروید (۱۸۵۶-۱۹۳۹)، متولد فرایبرگ، موراویا، روانشناسی مدرن را متحول کرد و درک بشریت از ناخودآگاه را برای همیشه از طریق توسعه انقلابی روان‌تحلیلی تغییر داد. فروید که در ابتدا به عنوان متخصص مغز و اعصاب در وین کار می‌کرد، پیشگام کاوش در خاطرات سرکوب شده، رؤیاها و امیال ناخودآگاه بود و پیشنهاد کرد که رفتار انسان تا حد زیادی توسط نیروهای ناخودآگاه و تجربیات کودکی هدایت می‌شود. نظریات انقلابی او شامل مدل ساختاری روان (شناسه، من و فرامن)، عقده اودیپ، و تفسیر رؤیاها به عنوان "راه شاهانه به ناخودآگاه" بود که با تأکید بر نقش محوری جنسیت در روانشناسی انسان، احساسات عصر ویکتوریا را به چالش کشید. علی‌رغم روبرو شدن با انتقادات و جنجال‌های قابل توجه در طول زندگی حرفه‌ای خود، به ویژه در مورد تأکید او بر تمایلات جنسی و روش‌های درمان، تأثیر فروید فراتر از روانشناسی بالینی گسترش یافت و عمیقاً بر ادبیات، انسان‌شناسی، جامعه‌شناسی، و فرهنگ عامه تأثیر گذاشت، و مفاهیم روان‌تحلیلی مانند مکانیسم‌های دفاعی، انتقال، و درمان گفتاری را پایه‌ای برای عمل درمانی مدرن و درک ما از سلامت روانی قرار داد.
train.tur: Moravya'nın Freiberg kentinde doğan Sigmund Freud (1856-1939), çığır açan psikanaliz geliştirimi aracılığıyla modern psikolojiyi devrimleştirmiş ve insanlığın bilinçdışı zihin anlayışını sonsuza kadar değiştirmiştir. Başlangıçta Viyana'da nörolog olarak çalışan Freud, bastırılmış anılar, rüyalar ve bilinçdışı arzuların keşfini öncülük etmiş, insan davranışının büyük ölçüde bilinçdışı güçler ve çocukluk deneyimleri tarafından yönlendirildiğini öne sürmüştür. Devrimci teorileri arasında psişenin yapısal modeli (id, ego ve süperego), Oidipus kompleksi ve rüyaların 'bilinçdışına giden kraliyet yolu' olarak yorumlanması yer alır ve insan psikolojisinde cinselliğin merkezi rolünü vurgulayarak Viktorya dönemi hassasiyetlerini sorgulamıştır. Kariyeri boyunca özellikle cinsel dürtülere verdiği vurgu ve tedavi yöntemleri nedeniyle önemli eleştiri ve tartışmalarla karşılaşmasına rağmen, Freud'un etkisi klinik psikolojinin çok ötesine uzanmış, edebiyat, antropoloji, sosyoloji ve popüler kültürü derinden etkilemiş, savunma mekanizmaları, aktarım ve konuşma tedavisi gibi psikanalitik kavramları modern terapötik uygulamanın ve ruh sağlığı anlayışımızın temel taşları haline getirmiştir.
train.ita: Sigmund Freud (1856-1939), nato a Freiberg, in Moravia, rivoluzionò la psicologia moderna e cambiò per sempre la comprensione umana della mente inconscia attraverso il suo sviluppo rivoluzionario della psicoanalisi. Lavorando inizialmente come neurologo a Vienna, Freud aprì la strada all'esplorazione dei ricordi repressi, dei sogni e dei desideri inconsci, proponendo che il comportamento umano sia largamente guidato da forze inconsce e da esperienze infantili. Le sue teorie rivoluzionarie includevano il modello strutturale della psiche (es, io e super-io), il complesso di Edipo e l'interpretazione dei sogni come la "via regia verso l'inconscio", sfidando la sensibilità vittoriana enfatizzando il ruolo centrale della sessualità nella psicologia umana. Nonostante abbia affrontato significative critiche e controversie durante la sua carriera, particolarmente riguardo alla sua enfasi sulle pulsioni sessuali e sui suoi metodi di trattamento, l'influenza di Freud si estese ben oltre la psicologia clinica, impattando profondamente letteratura, antropologia, sociologia e cultura popolare, rendendo concetti psicoanalitici come meccanismi di difesa, transfert e cura attraverso la parola fondamentali per la pratica terapeutica moderna e la nostra comprensione della salute mentale.
train.zho: 西格蒙德·弗洛伊德（1856-1939）出生于摩拉维亚的弗赖贝格，通过其开创性的精神分析学发展，彻底革命了现代心理学，永远改变了人类对无意识心理的理解。弗洛伊德最初在维也纳担任神经学家，开创了对压抑记忆、梦境和无意识欲望的探索，提出人类行为很大程度上由无意识力量和童年经历驱动。他的革命性理论包括心理的结构模型（本我、自我和超我）、俄狄浦斯情结，以及将梦境解释为"通往无意识的王道"，通过强调性在人类心理学中的核心作用来挑战维多利亚时代的敏感性。尽管在其职业生涯中面临重大批评和争议，特别是关于他对性驱动的强调和治疗方法，弗洛伊德的影响远远超出了临床心理学，深刻影响了文学、人类学、社会学和流行文化，使防御机制、移情和谈话治疗等精神分析概念成为现代治疗实践和我们对心理健康理解的基础。

train.explanation: British passenger liner that sank in 1912, becoming history's most famous maritime disaster
train.en: The RMS Titanic, launched in 1912 as the world's largest and most luxurious passenger ship, became history's most infamous maritime disaster when it struck an iceberg and sank during its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York City on April 15, 1912. Built by Harland and Wolff in Belfast and operated by the White Star Line, the "unsinkable" ship was a marvel of Edwardian engineering, stretching 882 feet in length and accommodating over 2,200 passengers and crew across three classes that starkly reflected the social hierarchies of the era. The tragedy, which claimed approximately 1,517 lives due to insufficient lifeboats and inadequate safety protocols, exposed the hubris of the age and led to fundamental changes in maritime safety regulations, including the establishment of the International Ice Patrol and mandatory lifeboat capacity for all souls aboard. The Titanic's story has transcended its historical significance to become a powerful cultural symbol, inspiring countless books, films, and documentaries, most notably James Cameron's 1997 blockbuster film, while the wreck's discovery in 1985 by Robert Ballard continues to fascinate researchers and the public, serving as both a time capsule of early 20th-century society and a sobering reminder of human fallibility.

train.en-arb: The RMS Titanic، launched في 1912 كأكبر وأفخم سفينة ركاب في العالم، became أسوأ كارثة بحرية في التاريخ عندما اصطدمت بجبل جليدي وغرقت أثناء رحلتها الأولى من ساوثهامبتون إلى نيويورك في 15 أبريل 1912. Built من قبل هارلاند وولف في بلفاست و operated من قبل وايت ستار لاين، السفينة "غير القابلة للغرق" كانت marvel للهندسة الإدواردية، stretching 882 قدماً في الطول و accommodating أكثر من 2200 راكب وطاقم across ثلاث طبقات التي reflected بوضوح التسلسل الهرمي الاجتماعي للعصر. The tragedy التي claimed حوالي 1517 حياة بسبب قوارب النجاة غير الكافية وبروتوكولات السلامة غير المناسبة، exposed غطرسة العصر و led إلى تغييرات جوهرية في لوائح السلامة البحرية، including تأسيس دورية الجليد الدولية والسعة الإلزامية لقوارب النجاة لجميع الأرواح على متنها. The Titanic's قصة transcended أهميتها التاريخية لتصبح رمزاً ثقافياً قوياً، inspiring كتباً وأفلاماً ووثائقيات لا تحصى، most notably فيلم جيمس كاميرون الضخم لعام 1997، while اكتشاف الحطام في 1985 من قبل روبرت بالارد continues يفتن الباحثين والجمهور، serving كـ time capsule لمجتمع أوائل القرن العشرين و sobering reminder للخطأ البشري.
train.en-tur: The RMS Titanic, 1912'de dünyanın en büyük ve lüks yolcu gemisi olarak launched, Southampton'dan New York City'ye maiden voyage'ı sırasında bir buzdağına çarpıp 15 Nisan 1912'de battığında tarihin en ünlü denizcilik felaketi became. Yetersiz can simidi ve yetersiz güvenlik protokolleri nedeniyle yaklaşık 1,517 can kaybına neden olan tragedy, çağın kibrini exposed etti ve denizcilik güvenlik düzenlemelerinde temel değişikliklere led etti, International Ice Patrol'ün kurulması ve gemideki tüm canlar için zorunlu can simidi kapasitesi including. train.en-hin: The RMS Titanic, launched 1912 में दुनिया की largest और most luxurious passenger ship के रूप में, became इतिहास की most infamous maritime disaster जब यह struck एक iceberg और sank अपनी maiden voyage के दौरान Southampton से New York City तक 15 अप्रैल 1912 को। Built Harland और Wolff द्वारा Belfast में और operated White Star Line द्वारा, "unsinkable" ship था एक marvel Edwardian engineering का, stretching 882 feet लंबाई में और accommodating 2,200 से अधिक passengers और crew को तीन classes में जो starkly reflected करते थे उस era की social hierarchies को। The tragedy, जिसने claimed लगभग 1,517 lives insufficient lifeboats और inadequate safety protocols के कारण, exposed किया उस age का hubris और led fundamental changes में maritime safety regulations के, including establishment International Ice Patrol का और mandatory lifeboat capacity सभी souls aboard के लिए। The Titanic की story ने transcended अपनी historical significance को become करने powerful cultural symbol, inspiring countless books, films, और documentaries, most notably James Cameron की 1997 blockbuster film, while wreck की discovery 1985 में Robert Ballard द्वारा continues fascinate करना researchers और public को, serving both time capsule के रूप में early 20th-century society का और sobering reminder human fallibility का।
train.en-ben: The RMS Titanic, launched 1912 সালে বিশ্বের largest এবং most luxurious passenger ship হিসেবে, became ইতিহাসের most infamous maritime disaster যখন এটি struck একটি iceberg এবং sank তার maiden voyage এর সময় Southampton থেকে New York City পর্যন্ত 15 এপ্রিল 1912-এ। Built Harland এবং Wolff দ্বারা Belfast-এ এবং operated White Star Line দ্বারা, "unsinkable" ship ছিল একটি marvel Edwardian engineering এর, stretching 882 feet দৈর্ঘ্যে এবং accommodating 2,200-এর বেশি passengers এবং crew তিনটি classes-এ যা starkly reflected করত সেই era এর social hierarchies। The tragedy, যা claimed প্রায় 1,517 lives insufficient lifeboats এবং inadequate safety protocols এর কারণে, exposed করেছিল সেই age এর hubris এবং led fundamental changes maritime safety regulations-এ, including establishment International Ice Patrol এর এবং mandatory lifeboat capacity সব souls aboard এর জন্য। The Titanic এর story transcended করেছে তার historical significance কে become করতে powerful cultural symbol, inspiring countless books, films, এবং documentaries, most notably James Cameron এর 1997 blockbuster film, while wreck এর discovery 1985 সালে Robert Ballard দ্বারা continues fascinate করে researchers এবং public কে, serving both time capsule হিসেবে early 20th-century society এর এবং sobering reminder human fallibility এর।

train.en-swa: The RMS Titanic, iliyozinduliwa mnamo 1912 kama chombo cha abiria kikubwa zaidi na cha kifahari duniani, ikawa msiba wa baharini wenye aibu zaidi katika historia wakati iligonga barafu na kuzama wakati wa safari yake ya kwanza kutoka Southampton hadi New York City tarehe 15 Aprili 1912. Ilijengiwa na Harland na Wolff huko Belfast na kuendeshwa na White Star Line, chombo hiki "kisichozamika" kilikuwa maajabu ya uhandisi wa Edwardian, kirefu futi 882 na kuwahudumia zaidi ya abiria 2,200 na wafanyakazi katika tabaka tatu ambazo zilionyesha wazi utaratibu wa kijamii wa kipindi hicho. Msiba huu, ambao uliharibu maisha takriban 1,517 kutokana na mashua za kuokoa zisizotosha na taratibu za usalama zisizofaa, ulifunua kiburi cha zama hiyo na kusababisha mabadiliko ya kimsingi katika kanuni za usalama wa baharini, ikiwa ni pamoja na kuanzishwa kwa International Ice Patrol na uwezo wa kulazimishwa wa mashua za kuokoa kwa roho zote zilizokuwa momboni. Hadithi ya Titanic imepita umuhimu wake wa kihistoria kuwa ishara yenye nguvu ya kitamaduni, ikichochea vitabu, filamu na nyaraka nyingi zisizohesabika, hasa filamu ya blockbuster ya James Cameron ya 1997, wakati ugunduzi wa mabaki yake mnamo 1985 na Robert Ballard unaendelea kuvutia watafiti na umma, ukitumika kama kizibo cha wakati cha jamii ya mapema ya karne ya 20 na kikumbusho cha kutisha cha makosa ya kibinadamu.
train.fa: آر.ام.اس تایتانیک، که در سال ۱۹۱۲ به عنوان بزرگترین و مجللترین کشتی مسافربری جهان به آب انداخته شد، زمانی که در اولین سفر خود از ساوتهمپتون به نیویورک در ۱۵ آوریل ۱۹۱۲ به کوه یخی برخورد کرد و غرق شد، به بدنام‌ترین فاجعه دریایی تاریخ تبدیل شد. این کشتی که توسط هارلند و وولف در بلفاست ساخته شده و توسط خط کشتیرانی وایت استار اداره می‌شد، کشتی "غیرقابل غرق" معجزه‌ای از مهندسی دوران ادوارد بود که ۸۸۲ فوت طول داشت و بیش از ۲۲۰۰ مسافر و خدمه را در سه کلاس جای می‌داد که به وضوح سلسله مراتب اجتماعی آن دوران را منعکس می‌کرد. این فاجعه که حدود ۱۵۱۷ جان را به دلیل کمبود قایق‌های نجات و پروتکل‌های ایمنی ناکافی گرفت، غرور آن عصر را آشکار کرد و منجر به تغییرات بنیادی در مقررات ایمنی دریایی شد، از جمله تأسیس گشت بین‌المللی یخ و ظرفیت اجباری قایق نجات برای تمام افراد حاضر در کشتی. داستان تایتانیک فراتر از اهمیت تاریخی خود رفته و به نمادی قدرتمند فرهنگی تبدیل شده است که الهام‌بخش کتاب‌ها، فیلم‌ها و مستندهای بی‌شماری بوده، به ویژه فیلم پرفروش جیمز کامرون در سال ۱۹۹۷، در حالی که کشف لاشه آن در سال ۱۹۸۵ توسط رابرت بالارد همچنان محققان و مردم را مجذوب می‌کند و هم به عنوان کپسول زمانی جامعه اوایل قرن بیستم و هم به عنوان یادآوری تلخ خطاپذیری انسان عمل می‌کند.
train.tur: 1912'de dünyanın en büyük ve en lüks yolcu gemisi olarak denize indirilen RMS Titanic, 15 Nisan 1912'de Southampton'dan New York City'ye ilk yolculuğu sırasında buzdağına çarparak batması ile tarihin en ünlü denizcilik felaketi haline gelmiştir. Belfast'ta Harland and Wolff tarafından inşa edilen ve White Star Line tarafından işletilen 'batmaz' gemi, Edward dönemi mühendisliğinin bir harikası olup, 882 fit uzunluğunda ve dönemin sosyal hiyerarşilerini açıkça yansıtan üç sınıfta 2.200'den fazla yolcu ve mürettebata ev sahipliği yapmıştır. Yetersiz can botu ve yetersiz güvenlik protokolleri nedeniyle yaklaşık 1.517 can kaybına yol açan bu trajedi, çağın kibir ve gururunu açığa çıkarmış ve Uluslararası Buz Devriyesi'nin kurulması ve gemideki tüm canlar için zorunlu can botu kapasitesi dahil denizcilik güvenlik düzenlemelerinde köklü değişikliklere yol açmıştır. Titanic'in hikayesi tarihsel önemini aşarak güçlü bir kültürel sembol haline gelmiş, sayısız kitap, film ve belgesele ilham vermiş, özellikle James Cameron'un 1997 yapımı gişe rekorları kıran filmi dikkat çekmiştir. Batığın 1985'te Robert Ballard tarafından keşfi araştırmacıları ve halkı büyülemeye devam etmekte, hem 20. yüzyıl başı toplumunun bir zaman kapsülü hem de insani yanılgıların ayıltıcı bir hatırlatıcısı olarak hizmet etmektedir.
train.ita: Il RMS Titanic, varato nel 1912 come la nave passeggeri più grande e lussuosa del mondo, divenne il più famigerato disastro marittimo della storia quando colpì un iceberg e affondò durante il suo viaggio inaugurale da Southampton a New York City il 15 aprile 1912. Costruita da Harland and Wolff a Belfast e operata dalla White Star Line, la nave "inaffondabile" era una meraviglia dell'ingegneria edoardiana, lunga 882 piedi e capace di ospitare oltre 2.200 passeggeri e membri dell'equipaggio attraverso tre classi che riflettevano nettamente le gerarchie sociali dell'epoca. La tragedia, che causò approssimativamente 1.517 vittime a causa di scialuppe di salvataggio insufficienti e protocolli di sicurezza inadeguati, espose la hybris dell'età e portò a cambiamenti fondamentali nelle regolamentazioni di sicurezza marittima, inclusa l'istituzione della Pattuglia Internazionale del Ghiaccio e la capacità obbligatoria delle scialuppe di salvataggio per tutte le anime a bordo. La storia del Titanic ha trasceso il suo significato storico per diventare un potente simbolo culturale, ispirando innumerevoli libri, film e documentari, più notevolmente il film blockbuster del 1997 di James Cameron, mentre la scoperta del relitto nel 1985 da parte di Robert Ballard continua ad affascinare ricercatori e pubblico, servendo sia come capsula del tempo della società dell'inizio del XX secolo sia come sobrio promemoria della fallibilità umana.
train.zho: 1912年作为世界上最大、最豪华的客轮下水的泰坦尼克号，在1912年4月15日从南安普敦驶往纽约市的处女航中撞上冰山沉没，成为历史上最臭名昭著的海难。这艘由贝尔法斯特哈兰德与沃尔夫造船厂建造、白星航运公司运营的"不沉之船"是爱德华时代工程技术的奇迹，长882英尺，可容纳2200多名乘客和船员，分为三个等级，鲜明地反映了那个时代的社会等级制度。由于救生艇不足和安全协议不当，这场悲剧夺去了约1517人的生命，暴露了那个时代的傲慢，并导致海上安全法规的根本性变化，包括建立国际冰川巡逻队和强制要求为船上所有人员配备救生艇。泰坦尼克号的故事已经超越了其历史意义，成为强大的文化象征，启发了无数书籍、电影和纪录片，最著名的是詹姆斯·卡梅隆1997年的票房大片。1985年罗伯特·巴拉德发现沉船继续吸引着研究人员和公众，既是20世纪初社会的时间胶囊，也是人类易错性的清醒提醒。

train.explanation: German composer and pianist who bridged the Classical and Romantic eras, creating some of history's greatest musical works
train.en: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), born in Bonn in the Holy Roman Empire, stands as one of history's most influential composers who revolutionized Western classical music by bridging the Classical and Romantic periods through his innovative harmonic language and emotional depth. Despite suffering from progressive hearing loss that began in his late twenties and eventually left him completely deaf, Beethoven composed nine symphonies, thirty-two piano sonatas, sixteen string quartets, and numerous other masterworks that expanded the scope and expressive power of classical music. His compositions, ranging from the jubilant "Ode to Joy" finale of his Ninth Symphony to the introspective late string quartets, demonstrated an unprecedented combination of technical mastery, structural innovation, and profound emotional expression that challenged conventional musical forms. Beethoven's personal struggles with deafness, unrequited love, and social isolation paradoxically fueled his creative genius, producing works of such universal appeal and enduring power that they continue to inspire musicians and audiences worldwide, cementing his legacy as a titan who transformed music from aristocratic entertainment into a profound art form capable of expressing humanity's deepest emotions and highest aspirations.

Despite suffering จากการสูญเสียการได้ยินแบบค่อยเป็นค่อยไป that began ในช่วงปลายวัยยี่สิบของเขาและ eventually left เขาหูหนวกสนิท, Beethoven composed เก้าซิมโฟนี สามสิบสองโซนาต้าเปียโน สิบหกสตริงควอเตต และ numerous masterworks อื่นๆ ที่ expanded ขอบเขตและพลังแห่งการแสดงออกของดนตรีคลาสสิก. His compositions, ranging จาก jubilant "Ode to Joy" finale ของ Ninth Symphony ของเขาไปถึง introspective late string quartets, demonstrated การผสมผสานที่ไม่เคยมีมาก่อนของ technical mastery, structural innovation และ profound emotional expression ที่ challenged รูปแบบดนตรีแบบเดิม. Beethoven's การต่อสู้ส่วนตัวกับความหูหนวก ความรักที่ไม่ได้รับการตอบสนอง และการแยกตัวจากสังคม paradoxically fueled อัจฉริยภาพทางสร้างสรรค์ของเขา, producing งานที่มี universal appeal และ enduring power เช่นนี้ที่ continue สร้างแรงบันดาลใจให้กับนักดนตรีและผู้ชมทั่วโลก, cementing มรดกของเขาในฐานะยักษ์ใหญ่ที่ transformed ดนตรีจากความบันเทิงของชนชั้นสูงเป็นรูปแบบศิลปะที่ลึกซึ้งที่สามารถแสดงออกถึงอารมณ์ที่ลึกที่สุดและแรงบันดาลใจสูงสุดของมนุษยชาติ.
train.en-arb: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827)، المولود في بون في الإمبراطورية الرومانية المقدسة، stands كواحد من أكثر المؤلفين الموسيقيين تأثيراً في التاريخ الذي revolutionized الموسيقى الكلاسيكية الغربية من خلال bridging الفترتين الكلاسيكية والرومانسية عبر لغته التوافقية المبتكرة والعمق العاطفي. Despite suffering من فقدان السمع التدريجي الذي began في أواخر العشرينات من عمره و eventually left إياه أصماً تماماً، Beethoven composed تسع سيمفونيات واثنتين وثلاثين سوناتا للبيانو وستة عشر رباعياً وترياً و numerous أعمال رائعة أخرى التي expanded نطاق وقوة التعبير للموسيقى الكلاسيكية. His مؤلفاته، ranging من الـ jubilant "Ode to Joy" خاتمة سيمفونيته التاسعة إلى الرباعيات الوترية المتأخرة الاستبطانية، demonstrated مزيجاً لم يسبق له مثيل من الإتقان التقني والابتكار الهيكلي والتعبير العاطفي العميق الذي challenged الأشكال الموسيقية التقليدية. Beethoven's صراعاته الشخصية مع الصمم والحب غير المتبادل والعزلة الاجتماعية paradoxically fueled عبقريته الإبداعية، producing أعمالاً ذات جاذبية عالمية وقوة دائمة التي continue لإلهام الموسيقيين والجماهير في جميع أنحاء العالم، cementing إرثه كعملاق الذي transformed الموسيقى من ترفيه أرستقراطي إلى شكل فني عميق قادر على التعبير عن أعمق مشاعر البشرية وأسمى تطلعاتها.
train.en-tur: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), Kutsal Roma İmparatorluğu'nda Bonn'da doğdu, tarihin en etkili bestecilerinden biri olarak stands eder ve Batı klasik müziğini devrimleştirdi, Klasik ve Romantik dönemleri arasında köprü kurarak yenilikçi armonik dili ve duygusal derinliği ile. Yirmili yaşlarının sonlarında başlayan ve sonunda onu tamamen sağır bırakan ilerleyici işitme kaybından suffering olmasına rağmen, Beethoven dokuz senfoni, otuz iki piyano sonatı, on altı yaylı kuartet ve klasik müziğin kapsamını ve ifade gücünü genişleten sayısız başka başyapıt besteledi. Dokuzuncu Senfonisi'nin neşeli "Ode to Joy" finalinden içedönük geç dönem yaylı kuartetlerine kadar ranging olan besteleri, geleneksel müzik formlarına meydan okuyan teknik ustalık, yapısal yenilik ve derin duygusal ifadenin eşi görülmemiş bir kombinasyonunu demonstrated etti. Beethoven'ın sağırlık, karşılıksız aşk ve sosyal izolasyonla olan kişisel mücadeleleri paradoksal olarak yaratıcı dehasını fueled etti, böyle evrensel çekiciliği ve kalıcı gücü olan eserler producing etti ki bunlar dünya çapında müzisyenleri ve dinleyicileri inspire etmeye continues ediyor, müziği aristokratik eğlenceden insanlığın en derin duygularını ve en yüksek özlemlerini ifade edebilen derin bir sanat formuna transformed eden bir titan olarak mirasını cementing ediyor.
train.en-kor: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), born 신성로마제국의 본에서, stands 역사상 가장 influential한 composers 중 하나로 who revolutionized 서양 고전 음악을 by bridging Classical과 Romantic 시대를 through 그의 innovative harmonic language와 emotional depth로. Despite suffering 20대 후반에 시작되어 eventually 그를 completely deaf하게 만든 progressive hearing loss로부터, Beethoven composed 9개의 교향곡, 32개의 피아노 소나타, 16개의 현악 사중주, 그리고 numerous 다른 masterworks를 that expanded 고전 음악의 scope와 expressive power를. His compositions, ranging 그의 9번 교향곡의 jubilant "환희의 송가" finale부터 introspective late string quartets까지, demonstrated unprecedented combination을 technical mastery, structural innovation, 그리고 profound emotional expression의 that challenged 전통적인 musical forms를. Beethoven's 청각 장애, 짝사랑, 그리고 사회적 고립과의 personal struggles는 paradoxically fueled 그의 creative genius를, producing such universal appeal과 enduring power의 works를 that 그것들이 continue 전 세계의 musicians와 audiences를 inspire하기를, cementing 그의 legacy를 aristocratic entertainment에서 humanity의 deepest emotions와 highest aspirations를 expressing할 수 있는 profound art form으로 music을 transformed한 titan으로.
train.en-hin: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), born Bonn में Holy Roman Empire में, stands इतिहास के सबसे influential composers में से एक के रूप में जिन्होंने revolutionized Western classical music को Classical और Romantic periods को bridging करके through उनकी innovative harmonic language और emotional depth के। Despite suffering progressive hearing loss से जो began उनके late twenties में और eventually left उन्हें completely deaf, Beethoven composed नौ symphonies, बत्तीस piano sonatas, सोलह string quartets, और numerous अन्य masterworks जिन्होंने expanded किया classical music के scope और expressive power को। His compositions, ranging उनकी Ninth Symphony के jubilant "Ode to Joy" finale से लेकर introspective late string quartets तक, demonstrated unprecedented combination technical mastery, structural innovation, और profound emotional expression का जिसने challenged conventional musical forms को। Beethoven के deafness, unrequited love, और social isolation के साथ personal struggles ने paradoxically fueled उनकी creative genius को, producing works ऐसी universal appeal और enduring power के साथ कि वे continue करती हैं musicians और audiences को worldwide inspire करना, cementing उनकी legacy को एक titan के रूप में जिन्होंने transformed music को aristocratic entertainment से एक profound art form में जो capable है humanity के deepest emotions और highest aspirations को expressing करने का।

train.en-swa: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), aliyezaliwa Bonn katika Ufalme wa Kiroma Takatifu, anasimama kama mmoja wa watunga muziki wenye ushawishi mkubwa zaidi katika historia ambaye alibadilisha muziki wa kimapokeo wa Magharibi kwa kuunganisha vipindi vya Classical na Romantic kupitia lugha yake ya muunganiko wa kivumbuzi na kina cha kihemko. Licha ya kuteseka na upotezaji wa uongozi wa polepole ambao ulianza katika miaka yake ya mwishoni mwa ishirini na hatimaye ukamwacha bubu kabisa, Beethoven alikomba simfoni tisa, sonata za piano thelathini na mbili, quartet za kamba kumi na sita, na kazi nyingine nyingi za bwana ambazo zilipanua upeo na nguvu ya kuelezea ya muziki wa kimapokeo. Vitumbuzo vyake, kuanzia tamati ya "Ode to Joy" ya furaha ya Symphony yake ya Tisa hadi quartet za kamba za mwishoni za kujitafakari, zilionyesha mchanganyiko usiopata kifani wa ustadi wa kiufundi, uvumbuzi wa muundo, na kuelezea kwa kina kwa kihemko ambacho kilipinga maumbo ya kawaida ya kimuziki. Mapambano ya kibinafsi ya Beethoven na bubu, upendo usiobadilishwa, na kutengwa kwa kijamii vilikichochea kwa njia ya kipingamizi uongozi wake wa uvumbuzi, ukizalisha kazi za mvutano wa kimataifa na nguvu ya kudumu ambazo zinaendelea kuhamasisha wanamuziki na hadhira duniani kote, na kuthibitisha urithi wake kama mkuu aliyebadilisha muziki kutoka burudani za kifahari kuwa aina ya sanaa ya kina inayoweza kuelezea hisia za kina za ubinadamu na matarajio yake makuu.
train.fa: لودویگ وان بتهوون (۱۷۷۰-۱۸۲۷)، متولد بن در امپراتوری روم مقدس، به عنوان یکی از تأثیرگذارترین آهنگسازان تاریخ شناخته می‌شود که موسیقی کلاسیک غربی را با پل زدن بین دوره‌های کلاسیک و رمانتیک از طریق زبان هارمونیک نوآورانه و عمق عاطفی خود متحول کرد. علی‌رغم رنج بردن از کاهش تدریجی شنوایی که در اواخر بیست سالگی‌اش شروع شد و در نهایت او را کاملاً ناشنوا کرد، بتهوون نه سمفونی، سی و دو سونات پیانو، شانزده کوارتت زهی، و شاهکارهای بی‌شمار دیگری آفرید که دامنه و قدرت بیان موسیقی کلاسیک را گسترش داد. ترکیبات او، از فینال شادمان «سرود شادی» سمفونی نهم تا کوارتت‌های زهی متأخر درون‌نگر، ترکیبی بی‌سابقه از تسلط فنی، نوآوری ساختاری، و بیان عاطفی عمیق را نشان داد که فرم‌های موسیقی مرسوم را به چالش کشید. مبارزات شخصی بتهوون با ناشنوایی، عشق بی‌پاسخ، و انزوای اجتماعی به طور متناقضی نبوغ خلاق او را تغذیه کرد و آثاری با جذابیت جهانی و قدرت پایدار تولید کرد که همچنان موسیقی‌دانان و مخاطبان در سراسر جهان را الهام می‌بخشد و میراث او را به عنوان غولی که موسیقی را از سرگرمی اشرافی به شکل هنری عمیق قادر به بیان عمیق‌ترین احساسات و بالاترین آرزوهای بشریت تبدیل کرد، تثبیت می‌کند.
train.tur: Kutsal Roma İmparatorluğu'nda Bonn'da doğan Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), yenilikçi armonik dili ve duygusal derinliği aracılığıyla Klasik ve Romantik dönemleri birleştirerek Batı klasik müziğini devrimleştiren tarihin en etkili bestecilerinden biri olarak durmaktadır. Yirmili yaşlarının sonunda başlayan ve sonunda onu tamamen sağır bırakan ilerleyici işitme kaybı yaşamasına rağmen, Beethoven dokuz senfoni, otuz iki piyano sonatı, on altı yaylı çalgılar dörtlüsü ve klasik müziğin kapsamını ve ifade gücünü genişleten sayısız başka başyapıt bestelemiştir. Dokuzuncu Senfonisi'nin coşkulu 'Neşeye Övgü' finalinden içe dönük geç dönem yaylı çalgılar dörtlülerine kadar uzanan besteleri, geleneksel müzik formlarına meydan okuyan teknik ustalık, yapısal yenilik ve derin duygusal ifadenin eşi görülmemiş bir kombinasyonunu sergilemiştir. Beethoven'in sağırlık, karşılıksız aşk ve sosyal izolasyonla olan kişisel mücadeleleri paradoks biçimde yaratıcı dehasını körüklemiş, müzisyenleri ve dinleyicileri dünya çapında ilham vermeye devam eden evrensel çekiciliğe ve kalıcı güce sahip eserler üretmiş, müziği aristokratik eğlenceden insanlığın en derin duygularını ve en yüksek özlemlerini ifade edebilen derin bir sanat formuna dönüştüren bir dev olarak mirasını pekiştirmiştir.
train.ita: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), nato a Bonn nel Sacro Romano Impero, si erge come uno dei compositori più influenti della storia che rivoluzionò la musica classica occidentale collegando i periodi Classico e Romantico attraverso il suo linguaggio armonico innovativo e la sua profondità emotiva. Nonostante soffrisse di una perdita progressiva dell'udito iniziata verso la fine dei suoi vent'anni che alla fine lo lasciò completamente sordo, Beethoven compose nove sinfonie, trentadue sonate per pianoforte, sedici quartetti d'archi e numerosi altri capolavori che espansero la portata e il potere espressivo della musica classica. Le sue composizioni, che vanno dal giulivo finale "Inno alla Gioia" della sua Nona Sinfonia agli introspettivi quartetti d'archi tardivi, dimostrarono una combinazione senza precedenti di maestria tecnica, innovazione strutturale e profonda espressione emotiva che sfidò le forme musicali convenzionali. Le lotte personali di Beethoven con la sordità, l'amore non corrisposto e l'isolamento sociale paradossalmente alimentarono il suo genio creativo, producendo opere di tale appeal universale e potere duraturo che continuano a ispirare musicisti e pubblico in tutto il mondo, cementando la sua eredità come un titano che trasformò la musica da intrattenimento aristocratico in una forma d'arte profonda capace di esprimere le emozioni più profonde e le aspirazioni più elevate dell'umanità.
train.zho: 路德维希·凡·贝多芬（1770-1827）出生于神圣罗马帝国的波恩，是历史上最具影响力的作曲家之一，他通过创新的和声语言和情感深度连接古典主义和浪漫主义时期，彻底革命了西方古典音乐。尽管从二十多岁开始遭受渐进性听力丧失，最终完全失聪，贝多芬仍创作了九首交响曲、三十二首钢琴奏鸣曲、十六首弦乐四重奏以及众多其他杰作，扩展了古典音乐的范围和表现力。他的作品从第九交响曲欢欣鼓舞的"欢乐颂"终曲到内省的晚期弦乐四重奏，展现了技术掌握、结构创新和深刻情感表达的前所未有的结合，挑战了传统的音乐形式。贝多芬与失聪、单恋和社会孤立的个人斗争反而激发了他的创作天赋，创作出具有普世吸引力和持久力量的作品，这些作品继续激励着世界各地的音乐家和观众，巩固了他作为将音乐从贵族娱乐转变为能够表达人类最深层情感和最高理想的深刻艺术形式的巨人地位。

train.explanation: The world's first widely used antibiotic that revolutionized medicine and saved millions of lives
train.en: Penicillin, discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 through a fortuitous laboratory accident at St. Mary's Hospital in London, became the world's first widely used antibiotic and fundamentally revolutionized modern medicine by transforming previously fatal bacterial infections into treatable conditions. Fleming's serendipitous observation of a contaminated Petri dish, where the Penicillium notatum mold had killed surrounding Staphylococcus bacteria, led to the isolation of this "mold juice" that would become humanity's most powerful weapon against bacterial diseases. Despite Fleming's initial discovery, it wasn't until the early 1940s that Howard Florey and Ernst Boris Chain successfully developed methods for mass production, enabling penicillin's widespread use during World War II, where it saved countless soldiers' lives and earned the nickname "the wonder drug." The antibiotic works by disrupting bacterial cell wall synthesis, effectively causing bacterial cells to burst and die while leaving human cells unharmed, making it particularly effective against gram-positive bacteria including those causing pneumonia, scarlet fever, and wound infections. Penicillin's discovery ushered in the antibiotic era, dramatically reducing mortality rates from infectious diseases and paving the way for modern surgical procedures, while its development earned Fleming, Florey, and Chain the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, cementing its status as one of the most significant medical breakthroughs in human history.

train.en-zho: Penicillin, discovered 亚历山大·弗莱明在1928年通过在伦敦圣玛丽医院的偶然实验室事故, became 世界上第一个广泛使用的抗生素 and fundamentally revolutionized 现代医学 by transforming 以前致命的细菌感染为可治疗的疾病. Fleming's 对被污染培养皿的意外观察, 其中青霉菌已经杀死了周围的葡萄球菌, led 分离出这种"霉菌汁" that would become 人类对抗细菌疾病最强大的武器. Despite Fleming's 最初发现, 直到1940年代初 Howard Florey和Ernst Boris Chain才successfully developed 大规模生产的方法, enabling 青霉素在二战期间的广泛使用, 在那里它拯救了无数士兵的生命并earned "神奇药物"的绰号. The antibiotic works 通过破坏细菌细胞壁合成, effectively causing 细菌细胞爆裂而死 while leaving 人体细胞不受伤害, making 它对革兰氏阳性细菌特别有效 including 那些引起肺炎、猩红热和伤口感染的细菌. Penicillin's discovery ushered 抗生素时代, dramatically reducing 传染病死亡率 and paving 现代外科手术的道路, while 其发展使Fleming、Florey和Chain获得了1945年生理学或医学诺贝尔奖, cementing 其作为人类历史上最重要医学突破之一的地位.
train.en-jpn: Penicillin, discovered Alexander Fleming によって1928年に St. Mary's Hospital in London での fortuitous laboratory accident を通じて, became 世界初の widely used antibiotic となり fundamentally revolutionized 現代医学を previously fatal bacterial infections を treatable conditions に transforming することによって. train.en-tha: Penicillin, discovered โดย Alexander Fleming ในปี 1928 ผ่านอุบัติเหตุทางห้องปฏิบัติการที่บังเอิญ ณ โรงพยาบาล St. Mary's ในลอนดอน, became ยาปฏิชีวนะที่ใช้กันอย่างแพร่หลายเป็นครั้งแรกของโลก และ fundamentally revolutionized การแพทย์สมัยใหม่ by transforming การติดเชื้อแบคทีเรียที่เคยร้ายแรงถึงตาย เป็นสภาวะที่รักษาได้. Fleming's การสังเกตโดยบังเอิญของ contaminated Petri dish ที่ Penicillium notatum mold ได้ฆ่า Staphylococcus bacteria ที่อยู่รอบๆ, led การแยกสาร "mold juice" นี้ that would become อาวุธที่ทรงพลังที่สุดของมนุษยชาติต่อต้านโรคแบคทีเรีย. Despite Fleming's การค้นพบเริ่มแรก, มันไม่ได้เป็นจนกระทั่ง early 1940s ที่ Howard Florey และ Ernst Boris Chain successfully developed วิธีการสำหรับ mass production, enabling การใช้ penicillin อย่างแพร่หลายระหว่าง World War II ที่มันช่วยชีวิตทหารนับไม่ถ้วนและ earned ชื่อเล่น "wonder drug." The antibiotic works โดยขัดขวาง bacterial cell wall synthesis, effectively causing เซลล์แบคทีเรียระเบิดและตาย while leaving เซลล์มนุษย์ไม่เป็นอันตราย, making มันมีประสิทธิภาพโดยเฉพาะต่อ gram-positive bacteria including ที่ทำให้เกิดปอดบวม ไข้แดง และการติดเชื้อบาดแผล. Penicillin's การค้นพบ ushered ยุคยาปฏิชีวนะ, dramatically reducing อัตราการตายจากโรคติดเชื้อ และ paving ทางสำหรับการผ่าตัดสมัยใหม่, while การพัฒนาของมัน earned Fleming, Florey และ Chain รางวัลโนเบลสาขาสรีรวิทยาหรือการแพทย์ปี 1945, cementing สถานะของมันเป็นหนึ่งในความก้าวหน้าทางการแพทย์ที่สำคัญที่สุดในประวัติศาสตร์มนุษย์.
train.en-arb: Penicillin، اكتشفه ألكسندر فليمنغ عام 1928 من خلال حادث مختبري محظوظ في مستشفى سانت ماري في لندن، became أول مضاد حيوي يستخدم على نطاق واسع في العالم و fundamentally revolutionized الطب الحديث من خلال تحويل الالتهابات البكتيرية المميتة سابقاً إلى حالات قابلة للعلاج. Fleming's ملاحظة عرضية لطبق بتري ملوث، حيث قتل عفن البنسيليوم نوتاتوم البكتيريا العنقودية المحيطة، led إلى عزل هذا "عصير العفن" الذي would become السلاح الأقوى للبشرية ضد الأمراض البكتيرية. Despite Fleming's اكتشاف أولي، لم يكن until أوائل الأربعينيات أن هوارد فلوري وإرنست بوريس تشين successfully developed طرق الإنتاج الضخم، enabling الاستخدام الواسع للبنسلين أثناء الحرب العالمية الثانية، حيث أنقذ حياة جنود لا حصر لهم و earned لقب "العقار المعجزة". The المضاد الحيوي يعمل عن طريق تعطيل تخليق جدار الخلية البكتيرية، effectively causing انفجار الخلايا البكتيرية وموتها while leaving الخلايا البشرية غير متضررة، making فعال بشكل خاص ضد البكتيريا الموجبة الغرام including تلك التي تسبب الالتهاب الرئوي والحمى القرمزية والتهابات الجروح. Penicillin's اكتشاف ushered عصر المضادات الحيوية، dramatically reducing معدلات الوفيات من الأمراض المعدية و paving الطريق للإجراءات الجراحية الحديثة، while تطويره earned فليمنغ وفلوري وتشين جائزة نوبل في علم وظائف الأعضاء أو الطب عام 1945، cementing مكانته كواحد من أهم الاختراقات الطبية في تاريخ البشرية.
train.en-tur: Penicillin, Alexander Fleming tarafından 1928'de Londra'daki St. Mary's Hastanesi'nde şanslı bir laboratuvar kazası yoluyla discovered, dünyanın ilk yaygın olarak kullanılan antibiyotiği became ve önceden ölümcül bakteriyel enfeksiyonları tedavi edilebilir durumlara transforming ederek modern tıbbı fundamentally revolutionized etti. Fleming'in kontamine Petri kabının serendipitous gözlemi, burada Penicillium notatum küfü çevredeki Staphylococcus bakterilerini öldürmüştü, bu "küf suyunun" izolasyonuna led etti ve bu insanlığın bakteriyel hastalıklara karşı en güçlü silahı would become edecekti. Fleming'in initial keşfine rağmen, Howard Florey ve Ernst Boris Chain'in mass üretim için yöntemler successfully developed ettiği early 1940'lara kadar değildi, penicillin'in II. Dünya Savaşı sırasında widespread kullanımını enabling etti, burada sayısız askerin hayatını saved etti ve "mucize ilaç" nickname'ını earned etti. The antibiyotik bakteriyel hücre duvarı sentezini disrupting ederek works ediyor, effectively bakteriyel hücrelerin patlamasına ve ölmesine neden olurken human hücrelerini unharmed bırakıyor, onu pneumonia, kızıl hastalığı ve yara enfeksiyonlarına neden olanlar including gram-pozitif bakterilere karşı particularly effective making ediyor. Penicillin'in keşfi antibiyotik çağını ushered etti, enfeksiyon hastalıklarından mortality oranlarını dramatically reducing etti ve modern cerrahi prosedürlere way paving etti, development'ı Fleming, Florey ve Chain'e 1945 Fizyoloji veya Tıp Nobel Ödülü'nü earned ederken, onu insan tarihindeki en significant tıbbi atılımlardan biri olarak status cementing etti.
train.en-kor: Penicillin, discovered 알렉산더 플레밍에 의해 1928년 런던의 St. Mary's Hospital에서 우연한 실험실 사고를 통해, became 세계 최초의 광범위하게 사용된 항생제 and fundamentally revolutionized 현대 의학을 by transforming 이전에 치명적이었던 세균 감염을 치료 가능한 상태로. Fleming's 오염된 페트리 접시의 우연한 관찰, 여기서 Penicillium notatum 곰팡이가 주변 포도상구균을 죽였던, led 이 "곰팡이 즙"의 분리에 that would become 인류의 세균 질병에 대한 가장 강력한 무기가. Despite Fleming's 초기 발견에도 불구하고, Howard Florey와 Ernst Boris Chain이 대량 생산 방법을 successfully developed한 1940년대 초가 되어서야, penicillin의 광범위한 사용이 2차 대전 중 enabling되었고, 여기서 그것은 countless 병사들의 생명을 saved하고 "기적의 약"이라는 nickname을 earned했습니다. The antibiotic works 세균 세포벽 합성을 disrupting함으로써, effectively causing 세균 세포들이 터져 죽게 하면서 human 세포는 unharmed 상태로 두어, 폐렴, 성홍열, 상처 감염을 일으키는 것들을 including한 그람 양성 세균에 대해 particularly effective하게 making합니다. Penicillin's 발견은 항생제 시대를 ushered하여, 감염성 질병으로부터의 사망률을 dramatically reducing하고 현대 외과 수술의 길을 paving했으며, 그 development는 Fleming, Florey, 그리고 Chain에게 1945년 생리학 또는 의학 노벨상을 earned해주어, 인류 역사상 가장 significant한 의학적 돌파구 중 하나로서의 status를 cementing했습니다.
train.en-hin: Penicillin, discovered Alexander Fleming द्वारा 1928 में through एक fortuitous laboratory accident St. Mary's Hospital में London में, became दुनिया का first widely used antibiotic और fundamentally revolutionized आधुनिक medicine transforming previously fatal bacterial infections को treatable conditions में। Fleming का serendipitous observation एक contaminated Petri dish का, जहाँ Penicillium notatum mold ने surrounding Staphylococcus bacteria को killed था, led इस "mold juice" के isolation को जो would become मानवता का most powerful weapon bacterial diseases के against। Despite Fleming की initial discovery के बावजूद, यह नहीं था until early 1940s कि Howard Florey और Ernst Boris Chain ने successfully developed methods mass production के लिए, enabling penicillin का widespread use World War II के दौरान, जहाँ इसने countless soldiers की lives saved और earned nickname "wonder drug"। The antibiotic works bacterial cell wall synthesis को disrupting करके, effectively causing bacterial cells को burst और die while leaving human cells unharmed, making इसे particularly effective gram-positive bacteria के against including वे जो causing pneumonia, scarlet fever, और wound infections। Penicillin की discovery ने ushered antibiotic era को, dramatically reducing mortality rates infectious diseases से और paving way modern surgical procedures के लिए, while इसकी development ने earned Fleming, Florey, और Chain को 1945 Nobel Prize Physiology या Medicine में, cementing इसकी status एक के रूप में most significant medical breakthroughs मानव इतिहास में।
